lem-pe11-compact-self-adjoint-spectral-a:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space. Let $T:H\to H$
and $T_n:H\to H$ be compact, self-adjoint, nonnegative operators. Assume
$T_nx\to Tx$ in norm for every $x\in H$, $\sup_n\|T_n\|<\infty$, and the
family is sequentially collectively compact: for every strictly increasing
sequence $(n_j)$ and every bounded sequence $(x_j)$, the sequence
$(T_{n_j}x_j)$ has a norm-convergent subsequence. Then:

1. If $\mu_j>0$ are eigenvalues of $T_{n_j}$, $\mu_j\to\mu>0$, then $\mu$
   is an eigenvalue of $T$. Thus no positive spectral limit is spurious.
2. If $\mu>0$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $T$ with multiplicity
   $m=\dim\ker(T-\mu I)$, then for all sufficiently large $n$ the open
   interval $I=(\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta)$, chosen so that
   $\mu-\delta>0$ and $\overline I\cap\sigma(T)=\{\mu\}$, contains exactly
   $m$ eigenvalues of $T_n$, counted with multiplicity. Their distance to
   $\mu$ tends to zero, and the associated eigenspaces converge to
   $\ker(T-\mu I)$ in symmetric $H$-gap.

Here $\sigma(T)$ denotes the spectrum, and the symmetric gap between
finite-dimensional subspaces $E,F$ is
$$\max\left\{\sup_{x\in E,\,\|x\|=1}\operatorname{dist}(x,F),\ \sup_{y\in F,\,\|y\|=1}\operatorname{dist}(y,E)\right\}.$$
lem-pe11-hcurl-weak-limit:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open
set. Suppose $u_n\in H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$,
$u_n\to u$ strongly in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, and
$\sup_n\|\operatorname{curl}u_n\|_2<\infty$. Then a subsequence of the
curls converges weakly in $L^2$ to $\operatorname{curl}u$, the limit $u$
belongs to $H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$, and in fact
$u\in H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$.
def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected open set whose
boundary is locally the graph of a Lipschitz function (a bounded Lipschitz
domain). The zero-tangential boundary condition is the perfect-electric-
conductor (PEC) condition. We use PEC to name the closure convention below;
for a smooth field this is the usual condition $n\times u=0$ on the boundary.
Its space is
$$V:=H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega),$$
with the graph norm and closure convention of
[[def-na-hcurl-space]] and [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]]. For a positive
constant permittivity $\epsilon$ and a positive constant permeability $\mu$,
write
$$(u,v)_\epsilon:=\epsilon\int_\Omega u\cdot v\,dx,\qquad K:=\{u\in V:\operatorname{curl}u=0\},\qquad X:=V\cap K^{\perp_\epsilon}.$$
Thus $X$ removes the entire PEC curl kernel, without identifying that kernel
with a scalar gradient range.

For a bounded polyhedral subcase with a finite matching affine tetrahedral
mesh $\mathcal T_h$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], let
$$V_h:=N_h^1\cap V,\qquad K_h:=\{v_h\in V_h:\operatorname{curl}v_h=0\},\qquad X_h:=V_h\cap K_h^{\perp_\epsilon},$$
where $N_h^1$ is the lowest-order first-family edge space of
[[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. The notation for $K_h$ and
the $L^2$ quotient gauge follows [[def-na-curl-curl-kernel-quotient-gauge]],
restricted to this PEC subspace. The continuous PEC eigenproblem
is to find $\lambda>0$ and $0\ne u\in X$ such that
$$\mu^{-1}(\operatorname{curl}u,\operatorname{curl}v)_{L^2} =\lambda (u,v)_\epsilon\qquad(v\in X).$$
The discrete problem replaces $X$ by $X_h$ and tests against every $v_h\in X_h$.
The unquotiented PEC pencil on $V$ is to find $\lambda\ge0$ and
$0\ne u\in V$ such that the same weak equation holds for every $v\in V$.
The positive constants are homogeneous scalar coefficients. The coefficient
extensions to variable or tensor-valued media require their own weighted
compactness hypotheses and are not inferred from the unweighted PE09
discrete-compactness interface.
lem-pe11-zero-eigenvalue-is-curl-kernel:
## Statement

Let $V$, $K$, and the unquotiented PEC curl-curl pencil be as in
[[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]], with constant $mu>0$. For
$u\in V$, the weak eigenrelation at eigenvalue $0$ holds for every $v\in V$
if and only if $u\in K$. Thus the zero eigenspace is exactly the full PEC
curl kernel.
lem-pe11-gauge-space-infinite-dimensiona:
## Statement

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be any nonempty open set, let
$V=H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$, let
$K=\{u\in V:\operatorname{curl}u=0\}$, and put $X=V\cap K^\perp$ using
the $L^2$ inner product. Then $X$ is infinite-dimensional.
lem-pe11-smooth-nedelec-approximation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded
Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular refining family of matching affine
tetrahedral meshes $\mathcal T_h$, with maximum cell diameter $h\to0$. For
every $w\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, the canonical lowest-order
Nedelec edge interpolant $I_hw$, defined by its six oriented edge
circulations on each tetrahedron, is well-defined. For all sufficiently
small $h$ it belongs to $H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$, and
$$\|I_hw-w\|_{H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)}\longrightarrow0.$$
The edge moments are applied only to smooth fields here; this statement does
not extend them to arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ inputs.
lem-pe11-continuous-gauge-compact-embedd:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron
with connected boundary, and let $X$ be the full-kernel orthogonal gauge of
[[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]]. Every sequence in $X$ bounded in
$H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$ has a subsequence converging strongly in
$L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$. Equivalently, the inclusion of $X$, with its
$H(\operatorname{curl})$ graph norm, into $L^2$ is compact. Moreover there
is a constant $C_\Omega$ such that
$$\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \qquad(u\in X).$$
Thus the curl form is coercive on $X$ in its $H(\operatorname{curl})$ graph
norm.
lem-pe11-gauge-conforming-edge-approxima:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ and the shape-regular tetrahedral
family be as in [[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]]. For each mesh
let $K_h=\ker(\operatorname{curl}|_{V_h})$ and
$X_h=V_h\cap K_h^\perp$, with the $L^2$ inner product. Then for every
$u\in X$ and every sequence of mesh sizes $h_n\to0$, there are
$u_{h_n}\in X_{h_n}$ such that
$$\|u_{h_n}-u\|_{H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)}\longrightarrow0.$$
thm-pe11-edge-maxwell-spectral-approxima:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded contractible Lipschitz
polyhedral cavity with connected boundary. Let $\epsilon,\mu>0$ be constant
scalar coefficients and let $\{\mathcal T_{h_n}\}_{n\ge1}$ be a
shape-regular refining family of matching affine tetrahedral meshes, with
$h_n\to0$. Use the full continuous and discrete curl-kernel quotient gauges
$X$ and $X_{h_n}$ of
[[def-na-pe11-maxwell-cavity-eigenproblem]]. Suppose the three PE09
supplier statements on regular decomposition,
[[thm-na-discrete-compactness-and-poincare-lowest-order-nedelec]], and
[[thm-na-uniformly-bounded-commuting-cochain-projection]] hold for this exact
domain, boundary convention and mesh family. Then the continuous PEC curl-curl
problem has isolated positive eigenvalues of finite multiplicity. For every
isolated continuous eigenvalue $\lambda>0$ of multiplicity $m$, choose
$\delta>0$ so that $I=(\lambda-\delta,\lambda+\delta)$ has
$\lambda-\delta>0$ and its closure contains no other continuous eigenvalue.
Then $I$ contains exactly $m$ discrete eigenvalues for all sufficiently large
$n$; these converge to $\lambda$ and their eigenspaces converge to the
continuous eigenspace in symmetric $L^2$ gap. If positive discrete eigenvalues converge to a finite
limit, that limit is a continuous eigenvalue. Thus the method has no nonzero
spectral pollution. No claim selects convergent individual eigenvectors
inside a repeated eigenspace.

The positive coefficients in this theorem are homogeneous scalars. A
variable or tensor-valued coefficient requires a weighted compactness and
projection interface; it is not covered by the unweighted PE09 statements.
The quotient removes the entire curl kernel, so topology-dependent zero modes
are not counted as positive eigenvalues.
